highlights.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: A predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
highlights.summary: AlphaGenome Atlas maps the molecular effects of 9 billion single-letter DNA variants across the human genome.
body: How predicting the molecular impact of every possible single-letter DNA variant in the human genome will help accelerate our understanding of biology.

Today, we are introducing AlphaGenome Atlas: a platform containing predictions for the effects of 9 billion single-nucleotide variants — every single-letter change possible — in the human genome. It is the most comprehensive catalogue of how genetic mutations affect molecular biology, and it is available for academic research through an intuitive and free-to-use website portal.

DNA is the language of life. Mastering it is a grand challenge that could transform our ability to understand biology and treat disease. But progress has been limited by a fundamental problem: interpreting how genetic variations impact biology at a molecular level. With roughly 9 billion possible single-letter mutations in the human genome, testing each one in the lab is practically impossible.
points: AlphaGenome Atlas maps the molecular effects of 9 billion single-letter DNA variants across the human genome.

highlights.title: Ferrari vow to come back stronger after Monza 'failure'
highlights.summary: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says his team will head to this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid with "all the energy" to bounce back from their "failure" at Monza.
body: There were big expectations for Ferrari at their home event after Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were quick in Friday practice, only to miss out on the front row in qualifying before a dismal race on Sunday.
Hamilton dropped from fourth to 10th after going side by side with Leclerc at the first chicane, going through the gravel at Turn 2, which he was unhappy with.
Then Leclerc had a huge crash on the third lap which wrecked the car and left the Monegasque driver with initial eye issues.
Hamilton was up to third at one point in the race but lacked outright pace and finished sixth behind both Mercedes, Red Bull's Max Verstappen and both McLarens.

highlights.title: 5 Things Completely New to the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
highlights.summary: Nintendo gave players their first in-depth look at gameplay for the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake during today's Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. While the game's new graphical style got a lot of attention (love it or hate it), the company also revealed a number of new features.
body: Link can jump whenever he wants now. This might not sound like a big deal, but Nintendo made a big show of Link's newfound freedom. In the original Ocarina of Time, Link automatically jumped when he ran close to an edge, but outside that context he was largely bound to the ground. No more! Jumping is now bound to the X button and is one of the many ways Nintendo is making the nearly three-decade-old game more inline with modern gaming expectations. Furthermore, he can dash by holding down the A button. This is an improvement over the original game's strategy of rolling to speed traversal along.

Taking a page from Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, you can swap items with one button in the Ocarina of Time remake. The original game allowed some items to be assigned to buttons for easy access, but everything else had to be equipped by pausing the game. Now Link can cycle through all of his items with a simple button press. It might not be a glamorous new feature, but it sure does streamline the game and means you'll spend way less time in menus now.

highlights.title: Alice Zaslavsky’s satay-butter charred cabbage wedges with fragrant chicken mince – recipe
highlights.summary: The cookbook author has a shortcut method for blanching vegetables that saves on time, equipment and water. Check out more Alice Zaslavsky recipes. I love a burnt brassica, and there’s no better flavour than the big mama herself: the cabbage.
body: Vegetables in the cruciferous family, like brussels sprouts, broccoli and cauliflower, have naturally bitter compounds. However, with concentrated heat, this bitterness is transformed into sweetly caramelised corners and burnished bits.
It’s one way to make brassica boo-ers braver. But getting cooked-through cabbage with a softened heart and gnarly edges requires a delicate balance of time under heat.

Lucky for us, the sharp bitterness of cabbage has been bred out of more conventional styles on supermarket and greengrocer shelves. Modern varieties are much milder, sweeter and less fibrous, meaning they require far less cooking than the cabbages of old.
That’s why these days, I’m fond of a gentler method that softens their rawness without overcooking: the kettle-blanch.

highlights.title: Man Utd's £1bn rebuild faces toughest test
highlights.summary: Michael Carrick transformed Manchester United's fortunes after his appointment in January, steering the side from seventh to third and clinching their return to the Champions League.
body: But, after a disappointing start to the new campaign, how will they handle the challenge of juggling three games per week? And has their rebuild neglected one key part of their squad?
With no European football and early exits from the Carabao Cup and FA Cup against Grimsby Town and Brighton respectively, Manchester United only played 40 games in all competitions last term.
It was the joint-fewest of any Premier League side and the club's lowest total for a single season since the 1913/14 campaign.

The light schedule allowed Carrick to keep key players fresh while Manchester United's rivals were having to rotate. In the period between his appointment and the conclusion of the Premier League season, only five sides made fewer line-up changes than United.

highlights.title: Adobe is trying to make its AI generators idiot-proof in Premiere
highlights.summary: Adobe is overhauling how editors interact with AI in its Premiere professional video editing software. Its new Generative Media tool makes it easier to generate video, sound effects, music, and soundscapes without ever leaving the project timeline.
body: A dedicated Generative Media interface can now be accessed right from the project timeline.

Instead of jumping between browsers or external apps to find missing B-roll or audio elements, editors can now highlight an empty gap on the video or audio track and generate context-aware, fully editable clips without leaving the project. Editors can choose from multiple underlying models directly in the timeline — including Adobe Firefly, Google Veo, Runway, Luma, and Kling — to best match their project’s style.

Premiere is also getting new AI audio tools (in beta) that can separate overlapping speakers, automatically duck music under speech, and independently adjust dialogue and ambience. And Adobe is bringing its AI Assistant to After Effects (also in beta) that lets editors use plain-language commands to reorganize projects, fix technical problems, and create effects without writing expressions themselves.

highlights.title: Stop The Presses, Link Can Jump In Ocarina Of Time Remake
highlights.summary: Today, Nintendo aired The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. We learned the Ocarina of Time remake is launching November 5. We heard about a new orchestra concert touring the world in 2027.
body: At one point, the younger version of Link comes across a pond with rocks that he must jump across. In the previous Ocarina of Time game, Link would automatically jump when approaching the rocks. Now, however, players can make Link jump whenever they like, at the press of a button.

As Aonuma himself pointed out in the demo, jumping may not seem like a big deal, but because the original game didn't allow for free jumping, this is a major change in the context of Ocarina of Time. Though what was shown was faithful to the original, the combination of this jump mechanic and the new sprint mechanic could lead to some changes in level design in the final game.

The gameplay demo also showed off the remake's updated visual style through multiple locations from the Nintendo 64 classic, including the Deku Tree, Hyrule Market, and Kokiri Forest. Aonuma also revealed new Ocarina mechanics, including the ability to hum a tune or play it on a physical instrument and have it register through the Switch 2's built-in microphone.

Savvy Games Group: Brian Ward is stepping down as CEO of the Saudi-backed games conglomerate, with Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, taking over as interim CEO. Ward had led Savvy since 2021, overseeing a roughly $38bn investment push into the games industry that included the acquisition of Scopely and stakes in companies including Nintendo and Embracer Group.

Supercell: Lasse Seppänen has left the company after seven and a half years, most recently as GM of Supercell London, to pursue new game IP ventures, with plans to start his own studio in 2027. Seppänen previously worked on Everdale, Hay Day and Boom Beach, and ran Supercell’s central game production services before integrating Supercell London following its acquisition of Space Ape.
Separately, Luran Zhang has joined as community manager after nearly four years at Lilith Games working on Rise of Kingdoms, and Mateusz Janczewski has joined as game producer.

body: Naturally I’m thrilled to see soft serve has enjoyed a renaissance, especially in my city. Last year, cronut creator Dominique Ansel made waves with soft serve dipped in French butter. Soft serve margaritas took over TikTok this year. And if line culture is any indication of interest, soft serve spots like Culture and, in my neighborhood, Lisbonata, now draw round-the-block throngs of treat seekers.

Rather than spending hours (and a small fortune) waiting in line, I decided to see if I could spin up some decent soft serve in my own kitchen. But these machines, such as Ninja’s buzzy Creami Scoop and Swirl, can be pricey, and I couldn’t stomach the $349 cost for something we’d probably only end up using a few times a year (though the cult of Creami may argue it’s worth it ).

Enter Dash, a budget appliance brand known for its $11 mini waffle makers. I decided to try its line of ultra-affordable frozen dessert machines: the Soft Serve Ice Cream Maker, Deluxe Gelato & Ice Cream Maker and compact My Mug.

highlights.title: Google’s Atlas of the human genome could pave the way for new treatments
highlights.summary: Google DeepMind has unveiled an AI tool that its scientists claim could help unravel the mysteries of the human genome and transform our understanding of biology, accelerating scientific research and ultimately paving the way for new treatments for diseases.
body: DeepMind’s new AI-powered tool can learn patterns between DNA changes and our biology.
The platform, called AlphaGenome Atlas, contains a “predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome,” the researchers said in a blog post published on Tuesday.

DNA is written in an alphabet of four chemical “letters” — usually shortened to A, C, G, and T — and the human genome contains roughly three billion letter pairs. Those letters contain the instructions that make life work, such as how, when, and where genes are switched on and off, and to what degree. Changes to individual letters can be harmless, contribute to ordinary differences between people, or play a role in disease – a major challenge is figuring out which changes matter and how. It is a tough task as there are roughly nine billion potential single-letter substitutions.

body: Here's how to help Vicho and find the culprit in The Blood of Dawnwalker 's "A Study in Crimson" quest.

To obtain "A Study in Crimson" in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you must find Vicho. This quest isn't marked on your map, but the citizens of Svartrau City may have mentioned a "curio emporium" in passing. If you find, enter, and investigate this mysterious shop, "A Study in Crimson" will begin.
Beware that "A Study in Crimson" costs four time segments in total and can only be completed at night. If you run out of time, Vicho will ask you to come back the following night.

Vico's curio emporium is located just northwest of Svartrau Cathedral. Enter the city through the northeast gate, take the main road leading southwest, turn left at the first opportunity, and you'll find a shop with a notice of (temporary) closure nailed to the door.

highlights.title: Elon Musk told ex-girlfriend he needed ‘a legion of children before the civil war’
highlights.summary: Ashley St Clair was speaking at the Venice film premiere of Alex Gibney’s documentary Musk, where she warned of his dangerous influence. • Musk review – epic study of the world’s richest and most banal man.
body: Elon Musk is sowing “deliberate division” via his social media platform X that will be catastrophic unless regulated, the mother of one of the 14 confirmed children fathered by the world’s richest man has warned.

In Musk, a new documentary by veteran film-maker Alex Gibney, former Maga influencer Ashley St Clair says Musk told her in a text message he wanted to have a child with her because he needed to have “a legion of children before the civil war”.

The couple had a son in 2024 but have since separated. St Clair says Musk’s team offered her a $40m lump-sum payment and a monthly stipend of $100,000 in return for her signing a non-disclosure agreement but withdrew the offer after she refused to sign it.

Asked at the documentary’s Venice film festival premiere whether her ex-partner was just scared of a civil war or actively trying to stoke one, St Clair said: “Whatever it is, what he’s doing with this platform on X cannot be ignored, because he is stoking flames that don’t exist in the real world.”

highlights.title: Richard Kelly on Donnie Darko at 25: ‘It’s a Miracle That Any Movie Gets Made’
highlights.summary: The director discusses his debut novel, staying true to an artistic vision, and the absurd line of dialogue from Donnie Darko he believes will find its way into his obituary.
body: For a diehard fan of Donnie Darko, meeting director and screenwriter Richard Kelly is a thrill in itself. But to first encounter him as a silhouette in a darkened movie theater is to feel almost like a character in one of his films—unmoored by indefinite space and physics, questioning your altered perception.

It’s a hot Friday in mid-August when I sit down with Kelly, 51, at Santa Monica’s Aero Theatre, a beloved repertory venue that makes a key appearance in Donnie Darko, his remarkable debut feature. Released in October 2001 with virtually no marketing due to the tragic events of 9/11 weeks prior (the plot hinges on a plane accident), it couldn’t get a toehold at the box office. But in the months and years that followed, the film became a hit on the home video market and gained a fervent cult fandom thanks to its unique supernatural mystery.
points: The director discusses his debut novel, staying true to an artistic vision, and the absurd line of dialogue from Donnie Darko he believes will find its way into his obituary.

highlights.title: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
highlights.summary: Danijar Hafner’s office in San Francisco’s SoMa district sits mostly empty. His brand-new startup is still in stealth mode and doesn’t even have its name on the door. On the day I visit, there’s only one other person there, and little in the way of furniture. But what it lacks in decor, it makes up…
body: While Hafner, 31, won’t say too much about his new venture just yet, he describes it as a continuation of his longtime work to enable AI to navigate environments it has not encountered in training. The humanoids, which he imports from China, are the next evolution of this work—and its physical embodiment. Their ability to react in previously untested scenarios will be key to getting robots into human spaces. Because if you want to send a robot into a person’s home, for example, it needs to be able to handle a floor plan and furniture it’s never seen before.

To achieve this, Hafner relies on something called model-based reinforcement learning. He develops world models—AI models designed to emulate physical reality—and trains agents within them. The agent essentially treats the model as a real-world simulation and learns how to act there. It then uses those experiences to make predictions (to dream or imagine, Hafner might say) about future outcomes. That allows agents—or the robots they’re embedded in—to navigate unfamiliar situations IRL.
“I get to interact with a lot of really smart people in research at Google, and he easily sits in the top half of 1%.”

highlights.title: The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Missed A Giant Wind Waker-Sized Opportunity
highlights.summary: If you were hoping to see older Zelda games ported to or remastered for the Switch at the recent Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, you were likely disappointed, as Nintendo instead dedicated almost the entire show to its upcoming Ocarina of Time remake.
body: Out of all the Legend of Zelda remasters that have come to Switch consoles over the years, there's still a sizable Wind Waker HD-shaped hole in that collection. The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker HD released on the Wii U in 2013, with a number of upgrades compared to the original 2003 GameCube version.

While the original version of Wind Waker was added to the Switch Online GameCube library last year, the Wii U version is much better in comparison. It provides a smoother experience with various quality-of-life improvements, like a resolution boost, faster loading times, and subtle changes to the game that make it less of a chore to play in its second half. While it isn't considered as influential as Ocarina of Time, Wind Waker's impact can still be felt in modern Zelda games today.
The fact then that the upgraded version of one of the best Zelda games of all time is still only available on the Wii U is a shame. Much the same could be said of Twilight Princess HD on the Wii U.

body: “We made ‘Littermates’ to explore the strange, primal and often trivial relationship between siblings. At its heart, the film is an unconventional coming-of-age story set against a dystopian backdrop,” directors Scott Tinkham and Michael Woloson said in a statement. “We always imagined the film as something to experience with a crowd, so introducing it at Fantastic Fest and then bringing it to audiences around the country through Alamo Exclusives feels like the perfect way to start this next chapter.”
“Littermates” is the second film from Alamo Exclusives, following the documentary “Butthole Surfers: The Hole Truth and Nothing Butt.”

“’Littermates’ is exactly the kind of discovery Alamo Exclusives exists to champion. It’s funny, audacious, visually confident and nearly impossible to fit inside a conventional box,” Michael Kustermann, CEO of Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, said in a statement. “Through deadpan social absurdity and unnerving family dynamics, Scott and Michael have created a strange little world that is entirely their own. I can’t wait to introduce it to the Fantastic Fest fiends before bringing it to Alamo Drafthouse theaters nationwide.”

highlights.title: Curbs on vertical drinking in Soho pubs to go ahead as Khan criticises council’s ‘breathtaking arrogance’
highlights.summary: Exclusive: London mayor accuses council of ‘ignoring’ responses to a consultation. Sadiq Khan has criticised the “breathtaking arrogance” of Westminster council, which has kept restrictions on vertical drinking in Soho and an effective ban on new bars and pubs in the area.
body: The mayor of London has accused the Conservative-led council of “ignoring” the responses to a consultation into its new licensing policy. The vast majority of respondents, 81%, disagreed with the council’s “cumulative impact zone” which decrees that applications for bars and pubs in the West End of London, one of Europe’s most famous nightlife districts, will be refused unless in exceptional circumstances. Eighty-four per cent said the licensing policy would be bad for business.

Respondents also criticised the council’s position on “vertical drinking”, which is standing up to have a beverage, a common practice in British pubs. The council proposed, to widespread outcry, that new licences for pubs and bars should be granted to those venues which have table service instead of ordering at the bar, and those in which people are seated rather than standing.

The mayor had responded to a consultation held this summer by the council and ordered them to scrap the cumulative impact zone and allow pubs and bars to have space for vertical drinking. Andy Burnham, the prime minister, also waded into the row, saying vertical drinking is “British life”.

highlights.title: EV batteries last longer than drivers feared
highlights.summary: Electric vehicle batteries are lasting longer than previously feared by drivers, with most used EVs able to retain about 90 percent of their original usable battery capacity after 150,000 kilometers, a new study has shown.
body: Despite a surge in global EV sales on the back of rising fuel prices, long-term battery durability continues to be one of the key concerns for drivers when they consider switching from a petrol model to an electric car.
EV battery warranties typically cover eight years or 100,000 miles (160,000km) with car manufacturers required under the warranty to provide a replacement battery if capacity falls below 70 per cent.

According to the latest study published by Aviloo, an Austria-based group that analyzes battery health, the median state of health (SoH)—which represents the remaining percentage of a battery’s original usable capacity—for 20 popular EV models stood between 87 percent and 94 percent after 150,000 km.

The median SoH was between 91 and 97 percent after 50,000 km, and 88 and 95 percent after 100,000 km. The study was based on more than 500,000 tests Aviloo carried out globally on the 20 EV models including Tesla’s Model Y and Volkswagen’s ID.4 between 2022 and 2026.

highlights.title: Mistral raises €3B as sovereign AI becomes big business
highlights.summary: The French AI lab has raised €3 billion at a €21 billion valuation in a Series D round led by Samsung, Scaleup Europe and PSG Equity.
body: French AI lab Mistral AI on Tuesday said it has raised €3 billion (about $3.58 billion) at a post-money valuation of more than €21 billion (about $24.39 billion), confirming earlier rumors.

This Series D round, which Mistral said is “the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company,” was led by Samsung Electronics, with EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund and existing investor PSG Equity joining as co-leads.

Mistral said it will use the funding to scale its compute capacity, build infrastructure, accelerate commercial growth and expand its international footprint. The money could also help clarify its positioning — the company says its goal is not to build a European ChatGPT, and though its models haven’t gone mainstream, it still envisions itself as an AI lab.

The funding will help Mistral pursue a subtle shift in strategy that aims to further address concerns in Europe and elsewhere about being too dependent on the United States for tech, especially with the intensifying politics around AI regulation and products Stateside.

highlights.title: Battlefield 6 Redsec is borrowing yet another mode from Call of Duty: Warzone - Resurgence
highlights.summary: It's been argued that Battlefield 6 's Redsec battle royale off-shoot is a response to Call of Duty's popular Warzone mode, and today's news is another indication of that.
body: Battlefield Studios has unveiled Rapid Royale, Redsec's version of Warzone's Resurgence. If you're unfamiliar, Resurgence takes place on dedicated maps that are far smaller than the main mode's large playground, and offers many ways to respawn after death. The pace is significantly faster with more frequent firefights as a result, and these are the principles guiding the Redsec version, too.

Rapid Royale features a reduced player count and is likewise only available on maps smaller than the main mode's. The circles move faster, too, further pushing players closer and closer together. Expect matches that finish quickly, notably a lot shorter than the main mode.

Rapid Royale is one of several new additions coming to Battlefield 6 and Redsec with Season 5, which does not yet have a release date. While we wait for that, Season 4's final stage - named Tidal Strike - kicks off 15th September and introduces the first iteration of proximity chat.

As the name suggests, the feature allows players to communicate with others around them who are not part of their squad. It's initially available only in battle royale, with the plan to expand it to Battlefield 6 multiplayer down the road.

highlights.title: Safety for Whom? Refusing the Right Subset of a Topic, Not the Whole Topic
highlights.summary: A Blog post by Multiverse Computing on Hugging Face
body: Most safety alignment work treats harm as a property of a topic. A prompt is unsafe because it falls into a general category such as weapons, fraud, or self-harm, and guard models like LlamaGuard-3 encode exactly this kind of topic-level taxonomy. Benchmarks like XSTest and OR-Bench then probe the failure mode this creates, models that refuse safe prompts because they contain a dangerous-looking word, and refusal-calibration work tries to pull that number back down.

Our latest paper, Safety for Whom? Boundary-Aware Self-Distillation for Controlled LLM Safety Refusal, studies this narrower problem directly. The question is not whether an entire topic should be refused, but which subset of that topic is incompatible with a given deployment policy, and how to train and measure a model against that boundary.

Zelda creator Shigeru Miyamoto said you'll understand why the film has no subtitle after you see it. Miyamoto teased homages to the series and a big role for the Triforce, the latter of which is hardly surprising since it's a series cornerstone. You can catch the film in theaters on April 30, 2027, and Miyamoto said future updates about the film will be shared via Nintendo Today.
Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma showed off a look at the Ocarina of Time remake, specifically the early Kokiri Forest, and the release date. It's out on Nov. 5.

Aonuma gave a brief explanation of why the graphics look the way they do. Aonuma also teased a few new features, including minor-but-impossible-for-the-Nintendo64 changes like adding a jump button, letting you rotate the camera, and, a rather more interesting one, the ability to swim and dive without special clothing.

highlights.title: The New Chris Rock: The Comedy Icon on Directing ‘Misty Green’ and Not Returning to the Oscars Unless He’s Nominated
highlights.summary: Chris Rock isn’t exactly who you remember him to be. He likes to take his time. “What am I trying to say?” he asks himself repeatedly in conversation, pausing to truly consider that question before continuing to speak. And he doesn’t speak at all on an empty stomach.
body: That isn’t to say he’s shed the opinionated, incendiary persona that caught Eddie Murphy’s eye at a New York comedy club one night when Rock was just 19, leading to his being cast in Murphy’s “Beverly Hills Cop II” (1987) and later “Saturday Night Live” (1990-93). Rock was one of the few celebrities to publicly predict Donald Trump would win the 2016 election, and speaking about the president today, Rock says, “I’m not a fan. But it’s weird when somebody gets one thing right, and the one thing almost clears them of all their other sins. The news is fake. He got that right.”

Still, Rock has formed a habit of making concessions to his least generous interpreters before anyone has even criticized him. “People have their reasons, and nobody’s wrong,” he says after remarking that it’s difficult to find actresses interested in roles that involve nudity. Referencing some Black actors’ grievances about the prevalence of Brits and nepo babies in Hollywood — a position he disagrees with and satirizes in his upcoming film “ Misty Green ” — he says, “They’re valid. I’m not going to dismiss anyone.”

highlights.title: Want to borrow a dinosaur fossil? Try California’s one-of-a-kind taxidermy lending library
highlights.summary: A natural history museum lets residents take home 1,400 specimens, from bobcats and beetles to snakes in jars. On a hot afternoon in August, I walked out of the San Diego Natural History Museum carrying a whale rib, a leopard pelt, a taxidermized weasel and a small piece of fossilized dinosaur…
body: It felt like a heist. These were real specimens that belonged to the museum, not gift shop replicas. But for two weeks, they were mine to take home, display in my living room, even bring to events with my friends.

San Diego, California, has the only natural history museum in the US with a collection of nature specimens that they allow members of the general public to check out and take home, just like checking out books from a library.

Inside the museum, metal shelves of taxidermy fill the space floor to ceiling. Light glints off rows of plexiglass boxes: alert bobcats, their ears perked; birds posed on branches; a jackrabbit suspended in air as if in mid-leap. There are Riker cabinets filled with beetles and butterflies, shelves of pickled sea creatures and snakes in jars, and plastic bins of exotic animal pelts.
Haylie Priest, the loan program’s manager, guided me through the room’s wonders: 1,400 specimens in total, from a megalodon tooth fossil to a king cobra head in a jar.

videos.title: 216,000,000 Spy TVs | The LG Smart TV Problem
body: The LG Smart TVs we've tested have first-party ACR (automatic content recognition) functionality that can pry into your personal life with greater precision than you might realize, with LG Ad Solutions' executives and leadership saying, on camera, that LG "owns the glass." Not you -- even though you bought it -- but them. They also talk about knowing everybody in the household, knowing the secondary devices, moving from TVs to smartphones and other screens, and more in their B2B discussions. Beyond just the fact that we think the TV's native behavior parallels malware, the LG Smart TVs we tested also have a number of security vulnerabilities that can be exploited to convert the TVs into covert listening devices. In this investigation, we dive into the mix of LG's first-party functionality that (in our opinions) is tantamount to spying and LG's vulnerabilities and exploits that they have failed to protect against.
